title: POC playbook cheat sheet and deployment simulation
content:
Summary:
Quick, portable POC playbook for running a 1–2 week customer proof-of-concept. Focused on fast time-to-value: working demo, measurable metrics, and clear rollback/fallbacks. Use this as the single-page cheat-sheet during workshops and as the basis for the customer-run lab.

Context and desired outcomes:
- Customer: mid-market SaaS with document-processing workflow (redactions + summarization + search).
- Goal: validate 3 endpoints (summarize, redact, semantic-search via embeddings) at target p95 < 300ms for summaries (hosted model), embedding throughput 50 reqs/s, and end-to-end latency < 600ms for combined flow.
- Success criteria (must be clear for handoff to AE): functional demo + benchmark report + cost per 1k tokens estimate + runbook for production roll to Dedicated.

High level timeline (two-week compact):
- Day -3 to 0: environment prep (accounts, API keys, model choices).
- Day 1: Workshop (2h) — demo baseline, integrate sample client, collect example prompts.
- Day 2–3: Ingest and small-data evaluation (build prompt sets, embeddings).
- Day 4–6: Load tests + latency tuning (batching, cache live tests).
- Day 7: Midpoint review with customer; decide quantization / model variant for scale.
- Day 8–10: Harden routes, rollouts, and fallback policies; run chaos/regression tests.
- Day 11–12: Final demo, cost/latency report, handoff doc and next-steps.

Day-by-day quick tasks (cheat sheet):
- Day -3 to 0:
  - Provision demo workspace (account + sandbox). Assignee: Liam.
  - Create service tokens, KMS stub (if testing private). Assignee: Rita.
  - Preload 500 sample docs (split by type). Assignee: Ethan.

- Day 1 (Workshop): 2-hour agenda (script):
  - 0:00–0:10 quick intros + objectives
  - 0:10–0:25 baseline demo: summarize + redact + search (use sample doc set)
  - 0:25–0:45 guided integration: customer dev integrates SDK with a single endpoint
  - 0:45–1:20 hands-on: customer runs 10 prompts, annotates failures (notes to self: have prompt templates ready)
  - 1:20–1:50 tuning talk: batching, prefix caching, model variants (trade-offs)
  - 1:50–2:00 next steps and quick wins

- Day 2–3: Data & eval
  - Build 100 prompt pairs for regression tests (include edge cases).
  - Create embedding index (vector DB sandbox) and run similarity tests.
  - Automated eval harness: store outputs and diff against golden set (JIRA-ENG-2345).

- Day 4–6: Performance tuning
  - Run synthetic load tests: 1k concurrent clients, ramp to 50 req/s for embeddings.
  - Toggle batching window (50ms -> 200ms) and measure p50/p95.
  - Enable KV cache for repeated prefixes and test hit rate.
  - Note: measure cost delta when enabling 8-bit quantized variants.

- Day 7: Midpoint review
  - Present benchmark dashboard (latency, error rate, cost).
  - Decision checkpoint: proceed to scale plan or cut scope (if p95 > 3x target).

- Day 8–10: Hardening & rollback policies
  - Set rollout policy: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with auto-fallback to smaller model.
  - Create chaos scenario (region failover): simulate region 1 outage, verify routing to region 2.
  - Add alert thresholds: latency > 1s for 3m, error rate > 2% for 5m.

- Day 11–12: Finalize deliverables
  - Deliver final report: perf table + configs used + cost estimates.
  - Handoff folder: runbook, playbook, tickets for Dedicated sizing.
  - Postmortem notes: what failed during POC and what to fix for GA.

Task tracker (compact format — use in workshop):
- Integration: sample client + token auth + example SDK call. Owner: Liam. Status: unblock if token expired.
- Data ingestion: script to normalize docs (pdf -> text) + metadata. Owner: Ethan. Status: in_progress.
- Eval harness: automated diff and scoring (BLEU/ROUGE-ish + human labels). Owner: Rita. Status: todo.
- Load testing: k6 scripts + monitoring dashboard. Owner: Liam/Ethan. Status: todo.
- Rollout policy: config file for canary/fallback (yaml). Owner: Rita. Status: todo.

Risk register (quick):
- Risk: Customer data contains PII and cannot leave VPC. Mitigation: run Private stub, redact locally before any API call; require customer sign-off on redaction approach. Owner: Rita.
- Risk: Model latency exceeds target at realistic prompt sizes. Mitigation: precompute embeddings where possible, use smaller model variant for short queries, apply prefix caching. Owner: Liam.
- Risk: Unexpected token-cost increases in hosted mode. Mitigation: estimate token usage from sample set and include conservative 2x buffer; show 3 cost levers (batching, quantization, lower-context length). Owner: Maya.

Deployment simulation scenarios (these should be rehearsed during Day 8):
- Happy path (baseline): model A (float16) in region-us-west, sustained load 20 req/s, p95 180ms. Expected: no action.
- Degraded compute: GPU node slow after driver update. Action: route 20% traffic to model B (quantized) in region-us-east for 10 minutes. Observe perf and error spike.
- Region failover: region-us-west down -> traffic reroutes. Verify DB reads for embeddings are replicated and latency increases < 2x.
- Cost shock: sudden traffic spike increases estimated monthly cost > 25% of commit. Action: temporarily enable strict batching and limit concurrency for non-prod tokens.

Rollback & emergency playbook (short):
- If error rate > 5% for 5m: switch traffic to fallback model variant (smaller model) and escalate to SRE.
- If auth or KMS failure: revoke new tokens, use saved demo token in sandbox (rotate after incident).
- If embedding index corrupted: fall back to document search (TF-IDF) and mark incident for DB restore.

Monitoring and telemetry (what to collect):
- Per-route p50/p95 latency, request size (tokens in/out), model variant, region, cache hit rate, queue wait time, GPU utilization, token cost per request.
- Logs to include request_id, user_id (hashed), model_version, prompt_id.

Acceptance criteria (final handoff):
- Demo runs with 3 core flows working end-to-end with sample dataset.
- Benchmarks show p95 <= target threshold (or documented trade-offs).
- Cost estimate and recommended Dedicated sizing documented.
- Runbook checked into repo and customer has read-access to handoff folder.

Open questions / quick TODOs (for internal sync):
- Confirm whether customer requires E2E encryption at rest with HSM (ticketed to security).
- Need list of real document formats customer will test (pptx/odt?).
- Decide whether to include reranking endpoint in MVP (adds cost, helps precision).

Appendix: quick command snippets and config notes (for engineers)
- Sample SDK call (JS): redwood.client.generate({ model: 'rwd-llama-13b-f16', prompt: 'Summarize: ...' })
- k6 load ramp example: options { stages: [{duration: '2m', target: 50}, {duration: '5m', target: 50}] }
- Rollout YAML snippet: 
  rollout: 
    stages: [5,25,100]
    fallback: model-b-quantized

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep workshop code in repo branch poc/<customer>-<date>.
- Have a copy of the golden outputs for demo mode (so customer sees consistent results).
- Bring up cost calculator slide in first 10 minutes — customers care early.

Contacts and escalation:
- Solutions lead: Maya Thompson (owner)
- Platform SME: Liam Chen
- Data ingestion: Ethan Park
- Security reviewer: Rita Gomez

Next steps (immediate):
- Ship invite for workshop with pre-req checklist (Liam).
- Confirm sample data upload (Ethan).
- Create JIRA epic and link this doc (Maya).

---
End of cheat sheet. Keep this page minimal and copy key sections into the customer-facing delta doc before demo.
